The Mgr, Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co ... vs Gaddam Laxmi,
Karimnagar Dist And 7 ... on 21 July, 2023
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3695 Of 2014
Judgment:

entities.text:
Mgr, Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co ... vs Gaddam Laxmi,
Karimnagar Dist And 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present M.A.C.M.A is filed by the appellant/respondent No.3/Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, aggrieved by the order and decree dt.10.12.2013 passed in O.P. No.7 of 2012 by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional District Judge, Karimnagar at Jagtial (for short 'the Tribunal).

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional District Judge, Karimnagar at Jagtial
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the claim petition was filed by the petitioners for Rs.6,00,000/- on the account of the death of one Gaddam Adi Reddy (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased') and the Tribunal awarded Rs.4,95,000/- to the petitioners No.1, 4 to 6, and aggrieved thereby, the present appeal is filed by the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company.
4.
Heard both sides and perused the record.
2 RRN,J 5.

Learned Counsel for the Insurance Company vehemently argued that the vehicle involved in the accident is unknown even as per the FIR, but the vehicle was conveniently shown as involved in the accident.
He further contended that in this case, the driver or owner of the alleged crime vehicle was not examined to prove the involvement of the vehicle.
He further contended that the vehicle was under hire and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.
He lastly contended that the Tribunal failed to consider that PW.2 claimed to have witnessed the accident but was unaware of the vehicle number.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners had contended that the Tribunal was justified in fixing the liability on all the respondents but stated that the compensation awarded was meagre and prayed to enhance the same.

The Mgr, Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co ... vs Gaddam Laxmi, Karimnagar Dist And 7 ... on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37901203/
1 7.

entities.text: Mgr, Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins Co ... vs Gaddam Laxmi, Karimnagar Dist And 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the death of the deceased in a motor vehicle accident but the dispute is with regard to the involvement of the offending vehicle.

The learned Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company mainly contended that the vehicle involved in the 3 RRN,J accident is unknown even as per the FIR, but the vehicle was conveniently shown as involved in the accident.

The Tribunal while answering issue No.1 being "Whether the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.AP-15-AS-2509 by its driver?" had clearly discussed the issue by analysing the evidence of PW.2, who deposed that, on that day he was passing from the accident spot on his bike and at that time, the deceased passing in front of him on his bike and the offending Tractor driven by 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner giving dash to that bike from its back, due to which, the deceased having a fatal fall and his death taking place on the spot.

Subsequent to the registration of the FIR, the police conducted an investigation and found that the persons responsible for causing the accident are respondents No.1 and 2.
8.
Thus, the Tribunal was justified in answering the first issue in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
What remains to be decided is the scope of enhancement of compensation.
It is observed from the impugned order that only petitioners Nos. 1, 4 to 6 were awarded compensation but the claim made by the 2nd and 3rd petitioners was dismissed.

This decision of the Tribunal is 4 RRN,J also justified as the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 did not prove as to how they were the dependants of the deceased in spite of having their sources of income and keeping in view of their age.
The Tribunal granted Rs.4,68,000/- towards loss of dependency and the same is justified.
The Tribunal granted Rs.2,000/- towards transportation of the dead body and the same is also justified.

The Tribunal granted Rs.5,000/-, Rs.10,000/- and Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses,
loss of consortium and loss of estate.

However, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.77,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- + 15,000 + Rs.15,000/- + 10%) towards loss of spousal consortium, loss of estate and funeral .
9.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In all, the petitioner Nos.1, 4 to 6 are entitled to Rs.5,45,000/- towards compensation.

The appeal of the Insurance Company is devoid of merit and is liable to be dismissed, however enhancing the compensation to the petitioner Nos.1, 4 to 6 based on the principle of 'just compensation'.
1 (2017) 16 SCC 680.
5 RRN,J 10.
Resultantly, the M.A.C.M.A is dismissed.

However, in the facts and circumstances of the case,
the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.4,95,000/- to Rs.5,65,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh, Sixty Five Thousand only) with interest at 7.5% p.a.

The respondents are directed to deposit the compensation amount after deducting the amount, if any,
already deposited, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The manner in which the awarded amount to be apportioned is in the same ratio as directed by the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
